text: You ask an AI a question. Seconds later, an answer.
But it isn't pulling a finished reply from a file. It's predicting one, piece by piece.
With popular AI chat apps, your message travels to computers in a data center, running a large language model.
First, your text is split into tokens: small chunks like words, parts of words, or punctuation.
During training, the model learned patterns from huge amounts of text. It doesn't look through that text when it answers. The patterns are captured in billions of numbers.
Now it uses those patterns, and everything in the conversation, to calculate which token is likely to come next.
It picks one, adds it, and repeats, token by token, until the answer is complete.
That's why AI sounds so fluent. But fluent isn't the same as correct. It can sound confident and still be wrong.
So when an answer appears in seconds, remember: it was built one prediction at a time. Check what matters.
